see: Which festival was first?
is: Newport Jazz 1954 usually gets the credit, though Los Angeles had an annual jazz event from 1945.
anchor: Where did the music festival start?

see: Did people really boo Dylan at Newport?
is: Accounts differ; Wikipedia says a small number of purists booed and most reaction was enthusiastic.
anchor: What happened when Dylan went electric at Newport?

see: Who runs Newport Folk and Jazz?
is: The non-profit Newport Festivals Foundation, since 2011.
anchor: In New England: what Newport looks like now

see: How was Woodstock free if it had tickets?
is: The fences and ticket booths were not finished by opening day, so it became a free concert.
anchor: How many people went to Woodstock, and did it lose money?

see: What went wrong at Altamont?
is: A free concert in December 1969 where four people died, one of them stabbed near the stage.
anchor: What happened at Altamont?

see: Why is there no Glastonbury this year?
is: Glastonbury takes planned fallow years to rest the farm; 2026 is one.
anchor: Why does Glastonbury take a year off?

see: Why is Glastonbury's main stage a pyramid?
is: The first Pyramid Stage went up in 1971.
anchor: How did Britain end up with the camping festival?

see: Lollapalooza used to tour?
is: Yes, from 1991 to 1997, before settling in Chicago in 2005.
anchor: What was the touring festival?

see: Why is EDC in Las Vegas and not LA?
is: After a 2010 death, the LA Coliseum capped capacity at 75,000 a day and EDC moved in 2011.
anchor: Why is EDC in Las Vegas?

see: What happened to SFX?
is: It bought up dance promoters, went public in 2013 and filed for bankruptcy in 2016.
anchor: What happened during the EDM boom?

see: Is there a festival on a cruise ship?
is: Yes; music cruises such as Jam Cruise and Holy Ship! put the festival on a ship.
anchor: What kinds of festival are there?

see: What is the difference between a camping and a city festival?
is: Greenfield festivals build on open land with camping; urban ones use a park and sell by the day.
anchor: What kinds of festival are there?

see: Why are so many UK festivals cancelling?
is: AIF counted a record 78 losses in 2024 and blames costs; it wants a VAT cut on tickets.
anchor: Why are so many festivals being canceled?

see: Why did Pitchfork Fest end?
is: Its Chicago run ended in 2024; supporters blamed owner budget cuts, others a struggling market.
anchor: Why are so many festivals being canceled?

see: When did festivals come back after Covid?
is: US festivals returned in the second half of 2021; Glastonbury and Roskilde in 2022.
anchor: What happened to festivals during Covid?

see: Who actually owns this festival
is: Often a big promoter holding a controlling stake, with the founder still running it.
anchor: What does ownership change for a festivalgoer?

see: Is Lollapalooza a Live Nation festival
is: Yes, through a reported 51% stake in C3 Presents bought in 2014.
anchor: How did Live Nation end up with Lollapalooza?

see: Who runs Coachella
is: Goldenvoice, part of AEG Presents.
anchor: Who owns Coachella?

see: Who owns EDC
is: Insomniac, which formed a partnership with Live Nation in 2013.
anchor: How did Live Nation end up with Lollapalooza?

see: A European festival I like is owned by KKR
is: KKR bought Superstruct, which runs more than 80 festivals, in 2024.
anchor: What did KKR buy when it bought Superstruct?

see: My German festival tickets came from Eventim
is: CTS Eventim owns both ticketing and festivals such as Rock am Ring and Hurricane.
anchor: Where does CTS Eventim fit?

see: Is Glastonbury corporate now
is: It is family-owned; Neil Young has argued its BBC partnership amounts to corporate control.
anchor: Which festivals are still independent?

see: Who owns Boston Calling
is: MSG bought a controlling interest in 2016; by 2023 it was a Live Nation subsidiary, per the Boston Globe.
anchor: In New England

see: There are brand logos on every stage
is: Sponsorship is a major festival revenue line, often sold across several festivals at once.
anchor: Where does a festival's money come from?

see: Why is there a service charge on my ticket
is: Ticket service charges are listed as festival revenue by Live Nation.
anchor: Where does a festival's money come from?

see: How much does Coachella make
is: The last public gross was $114.6 million in 2017, per Billboard.
anchor: How much money does Coachella make?

see: Does Glastonbury make money
is: Yes: £5.9 million profit on £68.4 million revenue in 2024.
anchor: Does Glastonbury make a profit?

see: How much was the headliner paid
is: Rarely disclosed; Coachella 2017 headliners reportedly got $3-4 million each.
anchor: How much do festival headliners get paid?

see: Why isn't my favorite act playing a club show near the festival
is: A radius clause may bar it from playing nearby for months around the festival.
anchor: What is a radius clause?

see: Coachella was sued over its radius clause
is: Portland's Soul'd Out sued in 2018; the Ninth Circuit revived the case in 2020.
anchor: What happened in the Soul'd Out case?

see: Festivals keep getting canceled
is: Rising costs since late 2021 were named in a wave of 2024 US cancellations.
anchor: What does a festival spend money on?

see: Is a festival insured if it rains or is canceled
is: Usually yes for listed causes like weather; disease cover has been unavailable since COVID.
anchor: Do festivals have cancellation insurance for weather?

see: What happened at Fyre Festival
is: It was a fraud; its founder got six years in federal prison in 2018.
anchor: What happened to Fyre Festival?

see: Why did Woodstock 50 never happen
is: Its financier, Dentsu Aegis, pulled more than $18 million in April 2019.
anchor: What happened to Woodstock 50?

see: What has Astroworld cost Live Nation
is: A $186 million charge beyond insurance in Q1 2024, plus settlements of all 10 wrongful-death suits.
anchor: What has Astroworld cost?

see: Why is the headliner's name so big on the poster
is: Font size and line position are billing, which signals status and is negotiated by agents.
anchor: Why are some names bigger on the poster?

see: The lineup is in alphabetical order
is: Some festivals list A-Z, or A-Z within font-size tiers, to avoid placement fights.
anchor: Alphabetical or billing order: the IFF debate

see: Roskilde's poster has rows of different sizes
is: Roskilde uses 100/90/70/50/40% font tiers, alphabetical within each.
anchor: How does Roskilde size its poster?

see: The poster is a circle or crossword and I can't find anyone
is: Some festivals use unranked layouts on purpose so no one argues about order.
anchor: Why are lineup posters getting harder to read?

see: A band skipped my city all year after a festival booking
is: Radius clauses bar nearby shows for months around a festival date.
anchor: What is a radius clause?

see: Every festival seems to wait for Coachella's lineup
is: Coachella's contracts give it first right to announce in its region.
anchor: Why does one festival's announcement hold up another's?

see: The festival released a separate lineup for each day
is: That is the day split, usually out after the main poster.
anchor: What is a day split?

see: How far ahead do festivals book headliners
is: Often a year or more; some booking for next year starts while this year is still being booked.
anchor: How far ahead are headliners booked?

see: I got a loyalty presale code by text
is: Past buyers get the first and cheapest access window.
anchor: What is a loyalty presale, and how do you get one?

see: The ticket says Tier 1 or early bird
is: The cheapest limited tier; the price rises when it sells out.
anchor: What do "early bird" and "Tier 1" mean?

see: It says sold out but tickets are still on sale
is: Often only one tier or pass type sold out.
anchor: What do "early bird" and "Tier 1" mean?

see: Glastonbury wants my photo before I can buy
is: Glastonbury tickets are registered to a named, photographed person and are non-transferable.
anchor: How does Glastonbury sell tickets?

see: I can pay for my festival ticket in installments
is: Payment plans take a deposit now and the balance later; check the fees and missed-payment rules.
anchor: How do festival payment plans work?

see: Resale tickets cost four times face value
is: Without official face-value resale, secondary prices can jump within minutes.
anchor: Resale: face-value exchanges vs. open resale

see: The festival sold out before announcing anyone
is: Strong brands like Newport Folk and Tomorrowland sell out on reputation alone.
anchor: Can a festival sell out before announcing anyone?

see: The price changed while I was in the queue
is: That would be dynamic pricing; most festivals use pre-set tiers instead.
anchor: Do festivals use dynamic pricing?

see: The fees showed up at checkout
is: In the US, sellers must show the all-in price with mandatory fees up front since May 12, 2025.
anchor: Do festivals use dynamic pricing?

see: Why does the festival post a long recap video
is: The aftermovie is year-round marketing for next year's sale.
anchor: How do festivals advertise?

see: The stages go up weeks before the festival
is: Big stages can take nearly three months to build; Glastonbury's phone masts arrive in mid-May.
anchor: How long does it take to build a festival?

see: What is the Purple Guide
is: The UK's industry safety guide for outdoor events, published by the Events Industry Forum; guidance, not law.
anchor: What is the Purple Guide?

see: The toilet lines are always worse for women
is: UK guidance plans five times as many toilets per woman as per man, before urinals.
anchor: How many toilets does a festival need?

see: The water refill line is huge
is: Supply is half the job; tap numbers and placement are the other half, as Boston Calling found in 2024.
anchor: Where does a festival's drinking water come from?

see: I can hear generators everywhere
is: Most festival power is generators, increasingly running on HVO renewable diesel.
anchor: What powers a festival?

see: Why is there a fenced gap in front of the stage
is: That is the pit, where stewards and medics work behind a load-bearing barrier.
anchor: Why is there a gap between the crowd and the stage?

see: There are fences splitting the crowd into sections
is: Finger barriers and zoned pits divide big crowds into pens to stop surges building.
anchor: Why is there a gap between the crowd and the stage?

see: Does a festival need a license
is: Yes; UK councils license under the Licensing Act 2003, and US permits are local.
anchor: Does a festival need a license?

see: The crowd up front is so packed I can't move
is: Above about 5 people per square meter, people lose control of their movement.
anchor: How many people per square meter is dangerous?

see: What happened at Astroworld
is: Ten people died of compression asphyxiation on Nov. 5, 2021; no one was indicted.
anchor: What happened at Astroworld in 2021?

see: What happened at Roskilde with Pearl Jam
is: Nine young men died in a crush at the Orange Stage on June 30, 2000.
anchor: What happened at Roskilde in 2000?

see: What was the Love Parade disaster
is: 21 people died in a crush at the Duisburg event in 2010; the trial ended without a verdict.
anchor: What happened at the Love Parade in 2010?

see: The show stopped because of wind
is: Wind is the big risk to temporary stages; events set wind limits and stop the show when they are reached.
anchor: What happens when the weather turns?

see: Why did a stage fall down in Indiana
is: The roof failed in wind below its code minimum and its ballast was grossly inadequate.
anchor: Why did the Indiana State Fair stage collapse?

see: How many people go to the medical tent
is: About 13 in every 1,000 at Glastonbury 2022, mostly for joints, stomach trouble and blisters.
anchor: How many people end up in the medical tent?

see: They told us to shelter in place
is: It means stay where you are rather than try to leave, as at Burning Man in 2023.
anchor: What happens when the weather turns?

see: Why is free water such a big deal
is: Woodstock '99's $4 bottles in extreme heat made it a safety issue; UK guidance requires drinking water on site.
anchor: What did Woodstock '99 teach festivals about heat?

see: Why can't I bring my backpack
is: Bag rules tightened after 2017 and change by year; check the current official FAQ.
anchor: What can I bring, and why are bag rules so strict?

see: There's a drug checking tent at the festival
is: Licensed drug checking runs at some UK festivals; rules differ by country and state.
anchor: Is drug checking legal at festivals?

see: What is DanceSafe
is: A US nonprofit, founded 1998, that runs harm reduction booths with information, water and earplugs.
anchor: Is drug checking legal at festivals?

see: My wristband has a chip in it
is: An RFID chip carrying an ID number the festival looks up at each scan.
anchor: What is actually inside a festival wristband?

see: Is my wristband tracking me
is: Vendors say no GPS and no tracking between scanners; it logs each gate scan and purchase.
anchor: Do festival wristbands track your location?

see: The festival keeps telling me to activate my wristband
is: Registering links the band to you so a lost band can be frozen and its balance moved.
anchor: How do I activate my festival wristband, and why bother?

see: I can't get in again after leaving
is: Anti-passback: the gate needs an exit scan before it lets the band back in.
anchor: How do I activate my festival wristband, and why bother?

see: My wristband won't come off or loosen
is: It uses a one-way lock: tighter only, and cutting it voids it.
anchor: Why are some festival wristbands impossible to take off?

see: I cut my wristband by accident
is: Go to the box office with photo ID; replacements may cost a fee.
anchor: What happens if I cut my festival wristband?

see: Someone outside is selling wristbands cheap
is: Counterfeits fail the chip scan and get confiscated; arrests have followed at EDC and Ultra.
anchor: How to spot a fake festival wristband (and who gets caught selling them)

see: The bar only takes my wristband
is: A cashless system: a linked card or a festival-only balance on the chip.
anchor: How does cashless payment work at a festival?

see: I have money left on my wristband
is: Request a refund online inside the window; there is usually a small fee.
anchor: How do I get a refund of my cashless festival balance?

see: I missed the cashless refund deadline
is: The leftover credit is usually lost.
anchor: What happens to money left on a festival wristband?

see: My bag is too big for the gate
is: Bag sizes are set per festival; Boston Calling's 2023 limit was 6 x 9 inches.
anchor: What happens at the festival gate?

see: There's no phone signal at the festival
is: A city-sized crowd swamps the local towers; carriers bring cells on wheels.
anchor: Why is there no phone signal at festivals?

see: A truck with a tower on it parked by the field
is: A COW, or cell on wheels: a portable cell tower.
anchor: Why is there no phone signal at festivals?

see: Fields full of left-behind tents
is: About 250,000 a year are abandoned at UK festivals, per the AIF estimate.
anchor: What happens to tents left at festivals?

see: Love the farm, leave no trace
is: Glastonbury's slogan; it reports 99% of tents taken home.
anchor: How did Glastonbury get 99% of tents taken home?

see: A free bus from the train station
is: A ticket-holder shuttle, like Glastonbury's from Castle Cary.
anchor: How do I get to Glastonbury by train?

see: My ears are ringing after the festival
is: Likely a temporary threshold shift; earplugs cut it sharply in a 2016 trial.
anchor: Do earplugs really work at concerts?

see: Only empty water bottles allowed
is: Rules allow sealed or empty bottles so you can use free refill points.
anchor: Can I bring a water bottle to a music festival?

see: Raised platform by the stage for wheelchair users
is: An accessible viewing platform; companion limits vary by festival.
anchor: How does accessibility work at music festivals?

see: The ticket was the cheap part
is: All-in US trips were estimated at $800-$3,000 in 2024.
anchor: How much does it cost to go to a music festival?

see: Is most of a festival's carbon from people driving and flying there
is: Usually the largest share: up to 80% (2015 UK report) or 41% on average (2023 study).
anchor: Is audience travel really 80% of festival emissions?

see: How much carbon do UK festivals put out
is: About 100,000 tonnes CO2e a year including travel (2015 estimate).
anchor: How big is a festival's carbon footprint?

see: The generators say they run on HVO
is: A renewable diesel from waste oils; savings claims range from up to 90% to about half.
anchor: What is HVO, and why are festivals switching to it?

see: I can't buy a bottle of water at Glastonbury
is: Single-use plastic bottles have not been sold since 2019; cans and free taps instead.
anchor: Why did Glastonbury stop selling plastic bottles?

see: I paid extra for my beer cup at Roskilde
is: It is a 5 DKK cup deposit; return a cup and get 1 DKK back.
anchor: How do reusable cups work at Roskilde?

see: Can I leave my cheap tent behind
is: Please don't: an estimated 250,000 tents a year are left at UK festivals, mostly landfilled.
anchor: What happens to tents left at festivals?

see: Glastonbury isn't on this year
is: Fallow years rest the farmland; 2026 was one.
anchor: Why does Glastonbury take a year off?

see: The festival says it brought millions to town
is: Commissioned impact studies; methods differ, so figures aren't comparable.
anchor: How much money does a festival bring to a town?

see: Locals are renting their yards near Coachella
is: Indio regulates short-term rentals with permits, taxes and quiet hours.
anchor: Can you rent your house out during a festival?

see: I can hear the bass from my apartment miles away
is: Low frequencies travel farthest; UK targets come from the 1995 Pop Code.
anchor: How loud can a festival be near homes?

see: The music stops at 11pm
is: The UK Pop Code covers events between 9am and 11pm; local licenses set curfews.
anchor: How loud can a festival be near homes?

see: Why was Woodstock 50 canceled
is: The Town of Vernon denied its permit and rejected the appeal in July 2019.
anchor: Who decides whether a festival can happen?

see: What happened at Electric Zoo 2023
is: Day one canceled over missing permits; Sunday gate rush after reported overselling.
anchor: Who decides whether a festival can happen?

see: What is the Brockwell Park court case
is: Residents won a 2025 High Court ruling over Lambeth's use of the 28-day rule.
anchor: Who decides whether a festival can happen?

see: Can I get into a festival free by volunteering
is: Yes, via charities like Oxfam: three shifts, a refundable deposit, free entry.
anchor: How do you volunteer at a festival for free?

see: Is Roskilde a charity
is: Yes, a nonprofit that has donated 457 million DKK since 1972 (2026).
anchor: How do you volunteer at a festival for free?

see: Boston Calling was loud in Cambridge
is: 2017 sound bleed from Allston; the 2018 fix cut complaints nearly in half.
anchor: In New England

see: Is Newport Folk sustainable
is: Rhode Island's governor recognized it in 2023 for cutting single-use plastics.
anchor: In New England

see: When is festival season
is: A relay: the Southern Hemisphere in January to March, the US in spring, Europe June to August, Rio and the Gulf in September and December.
anchor: When is festival season, really?

see: What festivals are on in July
is: July is Europe's busiest month: Exit, Mad Cool, Awakenings, FIB, Tomorrowland and Fuji Rock in recent years.
anchor: The season month by month

see: Why is there no Glastonbury this year
is: 2026 is a planned fallow year; the farm rests roughly every five years.
anchor: Why is there no Glastonbury in 2026?

see: Did Tomorrowland happen after the fire
is: Yes - the main stage burned on July 16, 2025, and both weekends went ahead.
anchor: What happened to the Tomorrowland main stage in 2025?

see: Why does Tomorrowland have two weekends
is: To double the crowd to 400,000 without enlarging the site.
anchor: What happened to the Tomorrowland main stage in 2025?

see: Exit Festival left Serbia
is: Organizers cited financial and political pressure after backing student protests.
anchor: Why did Exit leave Serbia?

see: How big is Fuji Rock
is: 122,000 over four days in 2025, about 10% bought from abroad.
anchor: Japan and Asia: how big is Fuji Rock?

see: Splendour in the Grass canceled again
is: Skipped 2024 and 2025 amid rising costs and a headliner shortage; its site went up for sale.
anchor: Oceania: why was Splendour in the Grass canceled?

see: The same lineup is playing every Australian city
is: That is the touring circuit model Laneway uses.
anchor: Oceania: why was Splendour in the Grass canceled?

see: Biggest festival in South America
is: Rock in Rio, with over 11.2 million cumulative attendees since 1985 (reported).
anchor: Latin America: Rock in Rio and the Lollapalooza circuit

see: Festivals in Africa
is: Afro Nation began in Portugal in 2019; Nyege Nyege in Jinja, Uganda in 2015.
anchor: Africa: Afro Nation and Nyege Nyege

see: Biggest festival in the Middle East
is: MDLBEAST Soundstorm near Riyadh reported 180,000 on day one in 2021.
anchor: Middle East: how big is MDLBEAST Soundstorm?

see: How many people go to EDC
is: Over 525,000 across three nights in Las Vegas in 2024 (reported).
anchor: The US: EDC, Lollapalooza and the weather

see: Bonnaroo got rained out
is: Canceled after storms and flooding on June 13, 2025.
anchor: Why was Bonnaroo 2025 canceled?

see: People say Burning Man is not a festival
is: Its own Journal calls it a participatory city, with no official stages or schedule.
anchor: Is Burning Man a festival?

see: So many small festivals are closing
is: UK independents counted a record 78 losses in 2024 (AIF).
anchor: Elsewhere in the world: the 2024-2026 squeeze

see: Where did outdoor festivals start
is: Newport, Rhode Island, in 1954 is the usual answer, though Los Angeles had an annual jazz event from 1945.

see: Newport Folk sold out and they haven't said who's playing
is: It sells blind; 2026 tickets went in seconds before any lineup.
anchor: Why does Newport Folk sell out before the lineup is announced?

see: Someone famous showed up at Newport Folk unannounced
is: Surprise guests are a Newport Folk tradition (Dolly Parton 2019, Joni Mitchell 2022).
anchor: Why does Newport Folk sell out before the lineup is announced?

see: My Newport Jazz ticket costs $314.15, why the odd cents?
is: Official 2026 three-day price; odd cents look like fees folded in, not confirmed.
anchor: How much did Newport Jazz tickets cost in 2026?

see: Is Newport a company or a charity?
is: Both festivals are produced by the Newport Festivals Foundation, a 501(c)(3).

see: Did people really riot at a jazz festival?
is: Yes, in 1960: about 200 arrests reported and the National Guard called.

see: Why was Newport Jazz in New York for years?
is: After the 1971 fence crash it moved to New York in 1972, returning to Fort Adams in 1981.

see: Did they really boo Dylan?
is: Some did; who and why is still contested, per Wikipedia.

see: Where did Boston Calling go?
is: It skipped 2026 and plans to return June 4-6, 2027.

see: Boston Calling used to be at City Hall
is: It left City Hall Plaza after 2016 for Harvard's athletic fields in Allston.
anchor: How did Boston Calling start, and why did it leave City Hall Plaza?

see: Is Boston Calling owned by Live Nation?
is: By 2023 it was a Live Nation subsidiary, produced by C3 Presents, per the Boston Globe.

see: I can hear the festival from across the river
is: That's sound bleed; Boston Calling's 2017 sound carried into Cambridge.

see: Boston Calling 2024 was way too crowded
is: Boston EMS reported about 800 medical encounters; crowd numbers are disputed.

see: Is there a festival in Western Mass?
is: Green River in Greenfield and Wilco's Solid Sound at MASS MoCA in North Adams.

see: Do I need a ticket for the Pops on July 4?
is: No, the Boston Pops Fireworks Spectacular is free.

see: How far ahead do I need a permit for an event in Boston?
is: 10, 20 or 30 business days depending on tier; over 250 people is Tier 3.

see: Does my Boston event need a safety plan?
is: Yes if capacity is 1,500 or more: an Emergency Action Plan filed with OEM.

see: Why is a jazz festival called JVC?
is: JVC was the title sponsor from 1984 to 2008.
